---
title: "Configuration and API"
---

The pipeline should be configurable from YAML and callable from both the command line and Python. The implementation should infer which steps to run from the configuration when possible.

## Configuration principles

- Use YAML as the user-facing configuration format.
- Validate configuration with Pydantic or an equivalent schema layer.
- Support per-step configuration while allowing a single resolved configuration file per run.
- Record default values in `config.resolved.yaml` so reruns are reproducible.
- Validate conflicting choices before expensive computation starts.

## Example structure

```yaml
data:
  inputs:
    - /path/to/session_001
  probe: /path/to/probe.json
  debug_time_slice: null

raw_quality:
  enabled: true

artefacts:
  saturation:
    enabled: true
  stimulus:
    enabled: true

preprocessing:
  bad_channels:
    enabled: true
    multi_session_policy: union
  phase_shift: auto
  filtering:
    type: bandpass
    freq_min: 300
    freq_max: 6000
  common_reference: true
  whitening: true

sorting:
  sorter: kilosort4
  params: {}

postprocessing:
  waveforms: true
  quality_metrics: true

curation:
  gui: viewephys
```

## Command-line examples

Run the full pipeline:

```bash
ephys-pipeline run --config pipeline.yaml --output pipeline_run
```

Run only through preprocessing on a short time slice:

```bash
ephys-pipeline run --config pipeline.yaml --output debug_run --until preprocessing --debug-time-slice 0:120
```

Run one stage explicitly:

```bash
ephys-pipeline raw-quality --config pipeline.yaml --output pipeline_run
```

## Python API examples

A user setting up for the first time with a fast preprocessing iteration cycle:

```python
recordings = ["/path/to/session_001", "/path/to/session_002"]

preprocess(
    recordings,
    output_path="debug_preprocessing",
    time_slice="0:120",
    save_recording=False,
)
```

A user checking raw data quality metrics:

```python
recordings = ["/path/to/session_001"]

raw_data_metrics(recordings, output_path="raw_quality")
```

A user manually curating saturation artefacts:

```python
recordings = ["/path/to/session_001"]
detections = detect_artefacts(recordings, output_path="artefact_detection")
curate_artefacts(detections, output_path="artefact_curation", gui="viewephys")
```

## Best-practice warnings

A major benefit of a structured pipeline is that it can encode best practice directly into the execution path.

- For multi-session workflows, the same set of channels should be used across all sessions.
- If bad channels are removed before concatenation, the default policy should remove the union of all detected bad channels across sessions.
- Avoid re-running whitening or motion correction in the sorter if those steps have already been applied by SpikeInterface.
- Warn when a method was designed for high-channel-density probes and may behave poorly on smaller 32- or 64-channel recordings.
